objective: can you add more fluorophores to my platform? i want to have a wide cover more dyes, and FPs
assumptions: The active product is the web Planner. Classic runtime behavior remains parked; only src/microscopy_naming_assistant/markers.py is in scope because it is the web marker-KB source of truth.

The producer-to-consumer path remains src/microscopy_naming_assistant/markers.py -> tools/export_markers_kb.py -> web/kb/markers.json and web/kb.dev.js -> web/src/engine/kbpack.js -> web/src/engine/spectra.js -> panel, study-document, controls, and bench-card consumers -> dist/index.html.

The spectra v1 schema remains unchanged: overlapRules plus fluorophores; direct entries contain excitationPeakNm, emissionPeakNm, reviewStatus, and optional note; family entries additionally contain isFamily and variants; variant entries contain only excitationPeakNm and emissionPeakNm.
The current 300-900 nm plausibility range, emissionPeakNm > excitationPeakNm invariant, and data-driven 25 nm emission/20 nm excitation proximity thresholds remain unchanged.
This increment adds a balanced, microscopy-relevant cohort rather than claiming an exhaustive catalog.

Ratiometric, multi-state, or photoconvertible probes that cannot be represented honestly by one excitation/emission pair remain out of scope, including FURA2, BCECF, SNARF, JC-1, Indo-1, MitoSOX Red, and photoactivatable or photoconvertible fluorescent proteins.

Authoritative-source verification does not equal local experimental validation. New entries retain reviewStatus claude-drafted and the persistent UI warning until a microscopy specialist approves them.

Peak values are copied only from exact authoritative product/form records, FPbase records, or primary papers. Values are never averaged across solvents, conjugates, binding states, oxidation states, or pH states.
Generic loaders, resolvers, overlap scoring, and rendering are data-driven; production engine/UI changes are not planned unless regression tests demonstrate a concrete consumer defect.
Exact branded or numbered variants receive distinct canonicals or existing-family variants. Existing generic aliases must not silently collapse chemically distinct dyes or protein variants.
Pre-existing untracked .agents content is unrelated and must not be touched.

risks.risk: Vendor pages report different maxima for free dye, conjugate, bound form, solvent, pH, or oxidation state.
risks.mitigation: T1 records exact identity and context, prefers exact product manuals over overview tables, forbids averaging, and T9 enforces numeric parity between evidence and runtime data.

risks.risk: An exact name may already alias a generic canonical, producing incorrect resolution.
risks.mitigation: T2 audits the normalized alias index first; T8 requires zero multi-destination aliases and explicit generic-versus-variant tests.

risks.risk: The single-peak model can misrepresent ratiometric, multi-state, or photoconvertible probes.
risks.mitigation: Exclude incompatible probes, retain FURA2 as an explicit gap, document supported measurement states, and require a future schema decision before multi-peak additions.

risks.risk: Peak proximity is only a qualitative proxy for full spectral bleed-through.
risks.mitigation: Do not change thresholds or imply quantitative compatibility; retain the warning and threshold-driven regression cases.

risks.risk: A large content increment can hide omissions or source drift.
risks.mitigation: Use exact enumerated sets, split spectrum edits by category, generate marker mirrors, and enforce complete ledger-to-runtime equality.

risks.risk: Development tests can pass while the built artifact embeds stale KB data.
risks.mitigation: T12 regenerates immediately before build and verifies the served dist/index.html with representatives from every producer branch.
